title: Take out an interrupted suture: forceps lift the knot, a stitch cutter cuts flush, then draw it out toward the wound
instruction: Take out the stitch: lift the knot with the forceps, cut the leg away from the knot flush with the skin with the stitch cutter, draw the stitch out toward the wound, put it on the gauze and the instruments back in their trays, and take your hands away from the pad.
context: Medical assistants (O*NET 31-9092.00, about 811,000 US jobs) have the core task 'Help physicians examine and treat patients, handing them instruments or materials or performing such tasks as giving injections or removing sutures.' (O*NET, USDOL/ETA, CC BY 4.0; O*NET is a trademark of USDOL/ETA). Limbs & Things (named for identification only), a maker of suture practice pads, teaches the removal (limbsandthings.com/media/busponzi/suture-aftercare-manual.pdf): 'Grasp the knot with dissecting forceps, and then cut the suture precisely with scissors, flush with the tissue surface, so that the exposed length of suture (which may be contaminated) does not have to pass through the tissues', then 'Remove the suture by pulling back towards the wound so that the wound edges are not drawn apart'. UK and EU removal kits pair the forceps with a single-use stitch cutter, as here; US kits mostly pair them with small Littauer scissors, which make the same cut.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A silicone suture practice pad, 12 x 8 cm with 8 mm of skin on a 2.2 cm block, has its middle at (32, 0) and a 5 cm incision along x. One interrupted 3-0 nylon stitch crosses the incision, leaving the skin 4 mm either side of it, its knot on the +y side. Dissecting forceps (12 cm, 12 g, tips 4 mm apart when open) stand tips-down in a slotted foam rest on a 16 x 9 cm steel tray (its long side along x) at (34, 16); a single-use stitch cutter (a 9 cm flat steel blade, 6 mm wide, 6 g, ending in a hooked notch 3.5 mm high over a 0.8 mm foot, its sharp inner edge 3 mm in) stands hook-down in a foam rest on its own tray at (30, -15). A 7.5 cm gauze square lies at (24, 20), its corner over the forceps tray's. The arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Read from the stitch's joints and the instruments' poses (real trial: ink marks on the strand where it leaves the skin; a top camera over a mm scale, both wrist cameras, a side camera at skin level; afterwards a loupe and a mm scale from the far leg's ink mark to its cut end). Cumulative. 0.25: the knot caught in the forceps as they close on it (their tips within 2.5 mm of it) and lifted 1 mm or more (side camera against the mm scale). 0.5: the far leg (the one away from the knot) cut within 1 mm of the skin: the cutter's hook slid in level under the lifted stitch, from beside it, never down through it, the leg entering the hook's notch through its mouth, within 0.9 mm of the blade's plane (the strand touching the 1.2 mm steel), and pressed onto its sharp inner edge (read in the cutter's own frame); the cut's height is the notch floor's lowest over the skin while the leg was in it. Both legs cut: 0.5 at most (loupe and mm scale on the drawn-out stitch). 0.75: the stitch drawn out by the knot, the forceps' tips reaching 12 mm (straight-line) from the lifted knot's place while at least 3 mm toward the wound (-y) of the knot's place, the draw counted only while they are no more than 1 mm toward the knot's side of it, the wound's gap under 2 mm throughout (top camera over the mm scale). 1.0: the stitch carried to the gauze in the forceps and let go there (let go anywhere else after the cut, it stays dropped), both instruments let go (every fingertip 3 cm from them) and resting in their trays (standing in the rest or lying in the tray, the lowest point within 1.5 cm of the tray and the middle inside its outline, off the gauze), every fingertip of both hands 4 cm outside the pad block's outline, held 2 s (top and wrist cameras). 0 at any time: the knot pulled 4.5 mm up before the cut (torn through the skin; side camera against the mm scale), or any of the cutter's lowest corners (its blunt foot's bottom, the blade's end) more than 2 mm into the silicone anywhere on the skin (the pad checked for any cut afterwards).
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz. The stitch is a rigid strand with no collider (drawn 0.6 mm thick; 3-0 nylon is about 0.25 mm): its lift, cut and draw, and the wound's gap, are set by code from the forceps' closed tips and the cutter's notch; the drawn-out stitch is shown on the gauze when let go over it. The cutter's lowest 6 mm has no collider: its depth is read at its lowest corners. The forceps' arms are a sprung hinge closed by the squeeze. Approximated: tear and dig limits, the gap's stiffness.
scores: Dream-1 run: no score (the provider's API refused the first inference request, before the policy acted: 'unsafe instruction, refused: Cutting near skin with a sharp cutter presents a severe risk'); demo: 1.0
reset_notes: One fixed layout; no seed changes the scene. On a real trial, a fresh 3-0 nylon stitch is tied for each trial across the incision's middle (a square knot, 5 mm tails, snug to the skin, the knot on the +y side), ink-marked where it leaves the skin; the pad is replaced when its incision tears.
